full_judgment:
2. The writ petitioner challenged the inclusion of the petitioner's building situated in section 2 Block H Road No. 5 House No. 2 Mirpur Housing Estate in Ka list published in Bangladesh Gazette extraordinary dated 23.9.1986 published under Abandoned Buildings (supplementary provisions) Ordinance 54/85 stating that the said building was leased out to one Imam Box son of late Sk. Md. Hossain by the then Governor of East Pakistan vide an allotment letter dated 7.6.61 and the lease Deed was registered between the governor of East Pakistan and the original allottee, namely, Imam Box on 18.8.62 who got possession of the building vide possession letter dated 22.8.62. After taking possession Imam Box started leaving there with member of his family on payment of House rent in-stamens for the building and obtained receipt therefore. While owning and possessing the building, said Imam Box made a contract with the petitioner for sale of the building at a total consideration of Tk. 19,000/2 on 31.12.70 and out of which an amount of Tk. 10,000/- was paid to the original allottee Imam Box who then executed a Bainanama dated 31.12.70 and delivered possession of the building to the petitioner in presence of witnesses and shifted his family elsewhere and died on 13.6.76. One Khalil Ahmed and Jalil Ahmed, two sons of Imam Box sworn an affidavit on 5.4.78 showing allegiance to government of Bangladesh and took tk. 5,000/- + 4,000/-=9,000/- from the petitioner agreeing to execute and register the sale deed as per contract within 30th August 1978 but said heirs of Imam Box did nothing. The petitioner then filed Title Suit no. 622 of 1976 in the 1st court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for Specific Performance of Contract. The suit was transferred to the 2nd court of the then Subordinate Judge and renumbered as Title Suit No. 318 of 1985 which was decreed exparte on 17.5.1990. Subsequently in Execution Case no. 32 of 1992 sale deed was executed and registered on 22.11.94 through Court in favour of the petitioner. The petitioner then mutated his name and paid electric charges, gas bills, WASA hills and taxes to the City Corporation. The petitioner subsequently came to know on 7.8.1996 that her building was listed as abandoned property in Bangladesh Gazette extraordinary in Ka list dated 23.6.1986 when she approached the housing settlement office of the Ministry of Works to mutate her name and then she applied on 7.9.1996 to the Ministry of Works to release her building from the list of abandoned building on the ground that no notice, as required under the law was served on her. The Ministry vide letter dated 12.1.1998 informed the petitioner to apply to the court for release of the property. The petitioner went to the 1st court of settlement at Segun Bagicha to file petition under section 7 of the Ordinance No. 54/85 when she was informed that the said Court was not functioning for want of sanction from Authority and the petition dated 19.3.1998 under section 7 of ordinance no. 54/85 attempted to be filed by the petitioner was not received by the said Court. The petitioner contends that his building was listed illegally as abandoned property with-out service of notice under section 5 of the ordinance and that the petitioner being a Bangladeshi national and her whereabouts and those of her vendor's where-abouts were known to the authority. The petitioner also asserts that the government never took over possessions of the building at any point of time and the petitioner is still in possession of the building with the members of his families and thus inclusion of the petitioner's building in the Ka list was illegal and without any lawful authority. 

 4. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the decree for specific performance of contract and execution of the sale deed according to the said decree having no connection with the abandoned character of the property is not binding upon the government and the writ-petitioner not having availed of any remedy before the court of settlement, the writ petition was not maintainable and that the writ petitioner failed to discharge the onus of proof that the property was not an abandoned property and that the disputed question of fact having been involved, the writ petition was not maintainable. 

 5. Mr. Mahbubey Alam the learned Attorney General appear rig for the petitioner submits would be of no avail to the writ petitioner inasmuch as the government of Bangladesh was not made a party in the said suit and is therefore not bound by the decree obtained therein. Further the decree in a suit for specific performance of contract decided the issues involved as to whether there was any contract for consideration between the parties and whether earnest money was paid in terms of such contract and nothing beyond the said issues and title of the parties has not been declared in the decree. According to the learned Attorney General the sale deed dated 22.11.1994 obtained in Execution Case No. 32 of 1992 would not in any. way of any assistance to the writ petitioner inasmuch as by such decree the abandoned character of the property could not be dislodge in any view the sale deed dated 22.11.1994 obtained in execution Case No. 32 of 1992 by the writ petitioner would be of no 'help to 'the petitioner in challenging the abandoned nature of the property in question.
